correctness.rationale: Starting from the published two-stage sampling rule, conditioning on the first vertex class gives two probability laws \(Q_A\) and \(Q_B\). A classwise scaling changes only their mixture coefficient, proving the exact total-variation identity. Positivity and graph connectivity give weighted biregularity as the exact equality criterion. A missing bipartite edge supplies a nonzero polynomial witness, proving universal invariance only for complete bipartite graphs and a Lebesgue-null exceptional set elsewhere. Pairwise symmetric opinion updates depend only on the unordered-edge sequence, yielding trajectory-law invariance. The exact-rational checker passed 465 finite graph/edge checks; those do not replace the universal analytic arguments.

value.rationale: The node-weighted opinion model explicitly treats weights as measurable heterogeneities in activity. The theorem identifies exactly when a whole population-class activity scale is invisible to all unordered interaction and opinion observations, gives the precise sensitivity at other profiles, classifies exceptional weighted-biregular configurations, and quantifies what extra knowledge can restore identifiability. These are natural structural and inverse-modeling questions, and the iff classification extends to every connected bipartite graph rather than a narrow enumeration.
